_why: Three classes of tool the skills must handle deliberately. The linter (evals/lint-tool-calls.mjs) enforces all three. The GATED set is not listed here: it is read from evals/remote-tools.json, which evals/dump-transport-tools.mjs generates from the MCP server's own source. It used to be a hand-kept list of twenty and it was wrong for two months — see docs/incidents.md, 2026-09-17.

forbidden._why: Must never be called by any skill, on any transport. get_marketing_playbook is a second, contradictory methodology; get_bot_stats and get_suspicious_sessions because Sealmetrics does not give bot data, by product decision (2026-09-13). A mention passes only if its own sentence carries a refusal marker. get_channels was in this list until 2026-09-17 on the grounds that it '403s for every modern key'; the channel-groups router has accepted sites:read since PRD-055, so the claim was false and the ban enforced it. It is now under preferAlternative.

preferAlternative._why: Tools that work but are not the right default. A mention must name the preferred tool in the same block, so a reader cannot take the mention as a recommendation. `get_channels` has the same row fields as `get_top_channels` but wraps them under a `channels` key instead of returning a bare array, and neither accepts `compare` — so the compact one is the default because there is nothing to unwrap and nothing to get wrong. Verified against the live API on 2026-09-17: it returns data, not the 403 this file asserted for two months.

markers._why: A sentence naming a forbidden tool, or a tool the remote connector does not announce, must contain one of these, so that a reader (and a model) cannot mistake the mention for an instruction to call it. Deliberately tight: a bare `not` would pass `get_channels does not accept compare`, which is exactly the sentence that shipped a call to a tool believed to 403.
